distinguishing_features: A compliant polyurethane or polyurea layer is applied to the slurry-pump impeller rather than relying on hardening or replacement.
The proposed wear-reduction mechanism is elastic deformation and viscoelastic energy dissipation at the impact surface.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce quartz-particle erosion and material loss from a slurry-pump impeller.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded elastomer layer at the stated thickness is physically feasible and can resist abrasive slurry wear, although the stated greater-than-40% benefit and impact model are not established by the information provided.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Elastomeric protection is a familiar alternative for abrasive slurry service, making the choice of a compliant polyurethane layer a routine material option for an engineer addressing impeller erosion.
